meeting_header:
Date: 2026-03-24

summary: Weekly POC security sync focusing on SSO/SAML integration, audit logs/export, data retention and PII handling, SOC2 artifacts. Redwood to provide SOC2 report, audit log samples, and Okta/SAML checklist; Silverstone to confirm retention windows and network constraints for VPC peering.
transcript:
00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll try to keep to 30 minutes, uh 35 if needed. Maya from Redwood here, with Carlos from our SE team.
00:12 - John: Thanks, Maya. John Hayes joining from Silverstone, Priya and Marcus are on as well.
00:20 - Priya: Hi all. Quick note, we sent an updated list of compliance questions last night - did you folks get that?
00:28 - Maya: Yep, we saw it, thanks. We'll go through the highlights.
00:33 - Carlos: Quick agenda — SAML/SSO, audit logs, retention and masking, SOC2 artifacts and any open network items.
00:40 - Leah: Also curious about how long you keep search logs vs payloads — that's important for our retention policy.
00:48 - Maya: Great, let's start SSO. Marcus, are you the primary owner for Okta integration on your side?
00:55 - Marcus: Yes, I am. We're on Okta, SAML 2.0. We need to confirm metadata exchange and attribute mapping.
01:03 - Carlos: On our side we support SAML 2.0 and Okta out of the box. We'll provide an integration checklist (ACS URL, entity ID, cert thumbprint) and a sample metadata XML. There may be small naming mismatches on the attributes, e.g., our docs show 'email' and some IdPs call it 'mail', so we'll include mapping notes.
01:28 - Priya: Do you support SCIM for user provisioning?
01:31 - Maya: We do, but for the pilot customers often just SAML is used; we can enable SCIM if you want automated provisioning.
01:38 - Priya: For now SAML is fine. Also need RBAC controls — can we map Okta groups to RBAC roles?
01:45 - Carlos: Yes, group-to-role mapping is supported; we'll share a sample mapping table.
01:52 - John: Good. Next, audit logs — sample format would help. We need timestamped events, user IDs, API request ids, model variant used, and whether the payload contained masked PII.
02:05 - Carlos: We'll export a sample CSV with those fields; note there is a limit on how long we keep raw request payloads in hosted mode, but in private/Dedicated you can configure retention.
02:18 - Priya: That's an important point — we need to know default retention for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
02:23 - Maya: Default hosted retention for full payloads is 30 days, metadata/audit logs 90 days; Dedicated allows custom retention and with Private you control retention entirely. We'll send the retention policy doc.
02:38 - Leah: And for audit logs, is there a mechanism to push logs to our SIEM (Splunk/Datadog)?
02:44 - Carlos: Yes, we have push options — syslog/S3 export or direct API pulls, and also a streaming export to your S3 for ingestion. We'll include endpoints.
02:55 - Priya: On PII, can Redwood mask or redact PII at ingestion? We can't send raw PANs or SSNs.
03:02 - Carlos: We offer configurable redaction rules and a pre-ingest filter; for the pilot we can enable pattern-based masking. For stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can enforce no-payload-at-rest via customer-managed KMS.
03:18 - John: KMS — do you integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
03:21 - Maya: Yes, for Private we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM options). Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys but encryption at rest is enabled. We'll attach our key management doc.
03:34 - Marcus: Network — for VPC peering, we'll need an allowlist of IPs and outbound ports. Any constraints on port ranges?
03:43 - Carlos: We'll provide the IP ranges and ports. For Dedicated we typically use mutual TLS and peered VPCs; Private is fully in your VPC so less friction.
03:54 - Priya: SOC 2 — do you have Type II? Can you share the report and scope?
04:00 - Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II for the platform, we'll share redacted report and the control matrix. Also we did a recent third-party pen test and can share the exec summary.
04:12 - Leah: Do you have any FedRAMP or ISO?
04:15 - Maya: Not FedRAMP yet; we hold ISO 27001 in process, SOC2 is primary.
04:21 - John: About audit logs again — can we get a sample with elapsed latencies per request? We want to correlate to our transaction IDs.
04:28 - Carlos: Yes, we'll include latency fields and request IDs. Note that model variant field sometimes says 'gpt-like' or our internal alias which can be slightly different.
04:40 - Priya: On retention, are you able to set different policies for different customers or even different routes?
04:45 - Maya: Yes; Dedicated and Private allow per-route retention. For hosted there are org-level defaults and we can scope per-application with configs.
04:55 - Marcus: For testbench, can we pull logs programmatically? We want to run automated checks during the pilot.
05:01 - Carlos: Yes, programmatic exports via API and S3 push. We'll share sample curl and a small python snippet.
05:12 - John: Any limits on how frequently we can pull large logs?
05:15 - Carlos: There's rate limiting on the admin API; for large exports we recommend scheduled S3 batches.
05:24 - Priya: Regarding data residency, we need EU-only processing for certain datasets; do you support region scoping for model inference?
05:32 - Maya: Yes, we support region pinning; for EU-only you can run in our EU region or Private deployment inside your EU cloud. We'll note regions.
05:42 - Leah: About the logs again — retention for search logs vs payloads, can you purge them on-demand?
05:48 - Carlos: In Dedicated and Private yes, there's an on-demand purge API. For hosted we'll coordinate and can do retention overrides if contractually agreed.
06:00 - John: Ok, moving on, there's an item in our compliance questionnaire about immutable audit trail and export format.
06:07 - Maya: We can provide append-only audit logs with signed checksums in the export; we'll include an example.
06:14 - Priya: Also need to know access controls — is RBAC enforced via SCIM groups and can we get a list of admin roles?
06:21 - Carlos: Yes, admin roles include Org Admin, Security Admin, Billing, and Read-only Auditor. We'll send the role matrix and default permissions.
06:30 - Speaker 1: (unintelligible)
06:33 - Maya: Sorry, that cut out.
06:35 - John: For the pilot acceptance criteria — priya, you mentioned retention and redaction are big factors. Anything else?
06:42 - Priya: Performance and auditability. We need a clear SLA for latency percentiles and that logs are complete.
06:49 - Carlos: For Dedicated we'll commit p95 latency targets in the SLA; we'll propose a benchmarking plan to validate.
06:56 - Maya: Next steps recap: we'll send SOC2, pen test summary, SAML metadata, audit log sample, IP ranges, and retention policy.
07:05 - Leah: Can you also share an example of the audit log CSV?
07:08 - Carlos: Yes.
07:10 - John: Any blockers on our side to turn up Okta-based SSO for the pilot? Marcus?
07:15 - Marcus: We can share metadata and set up test users this week.
07:20 - Priya: We'll also confirm whether we need SCIM.
07:24 - Maya: Great. Anything else?
07:26 - Leah: No, that's it.
07:29 - Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
07:33 - End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mislabels (Speaker 1), a few truncated lines, and minor ASR errors.
